transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-31
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Sara Kim (Redwood AE), Miguel Torres (Redwood SE), Ellen Park (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Greenline Head of ML), Tom Reynolds (Eng Manager), Aisha Khan (SRE), Ben Cho (Data Scientist)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect): walkthrough of Redwood Optimize focusing on quantization profiles (INT8 / FP8), discussion of quality vs latency tradeoffs, suggested rollout and fallback policies, agreement to run pilot and share benchmark artifacts.

Topics: 1) INT8 vs FP8 quality delta 2) latency improvements and cost impact 3) per-model sensitivity and per-workload profiles 4) rollout/fallback strategies 5) next steps and pilot scope

Transcript:
[00:00] Sara: hey everyone thanks for joining, um quick intros? we have miguel and ellen from the eng team, i'll hand it to miguel to kick off with a quick high level on optimize.
[00:18] Miguel: yeah thanks sara, hi priya, tom, aisha, ben. so this session is a hands on walkthrough of Redwood Optimize quantization profiles. we'll show INT8 and FP8 tradeoffs, some perf numbers, and then talk about how you'd roll this out safely in your stack.
[00:36] Priya: great, our main ask is: we need to reduce token cost and latency for our RAG pipeline but not at the expense of answer quality, specially numerics and code snippets. we saw some artifacts with agressive quant in past.
[00:49] Tom: also SLOs — P95 latency needs to stay under 450ms for our user flows.
[00:55] Miguel: understood. quick framing: INT8 usually gives the biggest speedup and memory reduction, FP8 is often a nice midpoint — less quality regression but smaller gains versus INT8. our Optimize tool profiles your prompts and suggests per-model quant profiles, not just global.
[01:18] Ben: when you say profile, do you mean you run a sample of our prompts against candidates? do you need data redline?
[01:25] Ellen: good question. we do a local eval on an anonymized prompt sample you share. we only need the prompts and expected outputs for eval — you can scrub PII. the profiling job runs both quality and latency evals, and outputs a per-prompt delta.
[01:40] Aisha: what's the perf delta you typically see on the hardware you run? our infra uses Ampere A100-ish equivalent.
[01:48] Miguel: on A100 class, approximate headlines: FP8 gives ~1.2-1.4x token throughput vs FP32, INT8 often 1.6-2x depending on implementation and sequence length. latencies are workload dependent; short seqs get less gain. caveat: these are numbers at the model loop level — actual tail latencies include batching, kv cache warmup, etc.
[02:10] Tom: does Redwood support mixed precision per-layer? some of our older models were very sensitive in layer 1-3.
[02:16] Miguel: yes, our quant profiles can be per-layer or per-weight-group and Optimize will suggest which layers to keep in FP16/32. we've seen that keeping first MLP and attention heads in FP16 reduces hallucinations for some models.
[02:30] Priya: ok can you show the benchmark spreadsheet you mentioned?
[02:33] Miguel: sure — i'll share the live sheet after, but quick screenshot here: we ran Llama-2-13b, Mistral-7b, and RedPajama-INCITE-13B as a proxy. for our RAG prompt set INT8 reduced median latency from 320ms to ~190ms and cost per 1M tokens dropped ~40-45%. quality: mean opinion score drop was 0.08 on average for the L2-13b set, but for some prompt classes (code, math) the drop was larger. FP8 reduced latency to ~240ms with only ~0.02 average MOS drop.
[03:10] Ben: that matches our expectations. for numeric recall we saw big regressions with quant on 13b. do you have examples?
[03:18] Miguel: yes, we flagged specific prompts where INT8 introduced small numeric errors — we use a per-prompt regression threshold and then mark them to run in higher precision or use fallback model. so your production policy can say: if prompt is in "sensitive" bucket, route to FP16 or dedicated shard.
[03:35] Tom: routing adds complexity — how do you avoid a spike in cost when many prompts route to higher precision?
[03:41] Miguel: two levers: 1) caching + prefix caching for repeated queries reduces overall tokens to compute; 2) canary + gradual rollout: start with a small percent of traffic on INT8 and monitor quality regressions. Optimize also simulates expected cost impact of your fallback rules.
[03:58] Priya: can Optimize simulate tail latency? our main worry is P95 in real traffic, not median.
[04:04] Miguel: yes, Optimize runs latency distribution simulations using your seq-length histograms and a configured batcher; it outputs P50/P95/P99 estimates. we warn that synthetic bench vs live SLO can diverge due to network and app-side variability.
[04:20] Aisha: security question, where does the profiling job run? is our data leaving our VPC?
[04:26] Ellen: good callout — for hosted customers we do profiling in a controlled environment; for sensitive customers we offer Private profiling where the job runs inside your VPC or on-prem agent. we can also accept anonymized prompts. we'll put SOC2/ISO links in chat.
[04:40] Priya: and key management? we need KMS/HSM integration for any keys used.
[04:45] Sara: yes, Private supports KMS/HSM integrations and you retain key ownership, logs in your account — we'll share the compliance doc.
[04:52] Tom: how do you measure "quality" for the eval in Optimize? automated metrics or human eval?
[04:57] Miguel: mix. we run automated metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/EM where applicable, embedding similarity, hallucination detectors) and a small human MOS sample for edge cases. Optimize surfaces both automated deltas and sample outputs so you can do subjective checks.
[05:12] Ben: can we bring our own rubric? like precision recall for entity extraction?
[05:15] Miguel: absolutely. we let you plug in custom eval scripts and thresholds; Optimize will call them during the profiling run.
[05:22] Priya: show us the UI for per-route policies and rollout controls.
[05:25] Miguel: sure, switching to console view — (screen share) — here is the quant profiles tab: you can see suggested profile for each model/prompt cluster, estimated latency delta, and a quality risk score. you can click to configure rollout: percentage, canary users, fallback model, and alert thresholds.
[05:48] [screen content described] Miguel: for example this demo profile keeps first 2 layers in FP16, MLP weights in INT8, uses FP8 for attn weights. estimated P95 change: +10ms for FP8, -120ms for INT8 versus baseline.
[06:05] Tom: will this require a new model artifact or is it runtime-only?
[06:10] Miguel: mostly runtime-only — we generate quant parameters and runtime kernels. for some toolchains we also store a quantized artifact, but Optimize manages compatibility.
[06:20] Priya: what about model variants? e.g., if I want to pin to a redwood-verified variant?
[06:24] Miguel: we maintain verified performance profiles for curated open models; you can pin to those or upload your own model. Optimize will produce profiles for either.
[06:33] Ben: any difference in hallucination / coherency between L2 and RedPajama when quantized?
[06:38] Miguel: yes model architecture matters — some families are more robust. we've seen Mistral derivatives handle INT8 better for short-chat style, but for long-form reasoning Llama2 sometimes fares better with FP8. hence per-model profiling is key.
[06:55] Priya: show me an example regression table.
[06:58] Miguel: (shares table) here: prompt id, original score, int8 score, fp8 score, delta, suggested action (keep, fallback, partial fp). e.g. prompt_174: math problem, orig 0.98, int8 0.84, fp8 0.96, suggested: route to FP8 for this cluster.
[07:20] Tom: what's the rollout timeline you'd recommend for us? we have staging, canary, prod.
[07:25] Ellen: typical pattern: 1) run offline profiling on 200-500 prompts and get profiles (1 week), 2) staging rollout to 5% traffic with monitoring and automated rollback (1 week), 3) expand to 25% then 100% if no regressions. total ~3-4 weeks end-to-end for a conservative rollout.
[07:44] Priya: monitoring — what alerts do you integrate with? we use Datadog, and also have internal traces.
[07:50] Miguel: we have Datadog and Prometheus exporters, plus webhook alerts. Optimize emits quality regression events, latency SLO breaches, and cost anomalies.
[07:59] Aisha: what about cold-starts and kv cache impact for RAG?
[08:03] Miguel: good one — quantization doesn't change KV cache semantics but if you use a smaller variant for INT8 you might see different cache hit distributions. Optimize's sim accounts for cache warmup patterns if you provide access patterns.
[08:18] Ben: any gotchas for embeddings? we use embeddings for retrieval; quant affects generation, not embedding models, right?
[08:25] Miguel: correct — embeddings models are separate. Optimize currently focuses on decoder/generation quantization. we do have guidance on switching embedding models (distillation) but that's a separate flow.
[08:36] Tom: curious on economics — what cost numbers do you show? earlier you said 40% token cost drop for INT8 — is that total cost or just compute?
[08:44] Miguel: that's compute-side estimate. total cost depends on infra (network, storage) but compute is majority for token-heavy workloads. Optimize outputs both compute-only and estimated end-to-end costs based on your billing profile.
[08:58] Priya: are there any regulatory concerns if we use quantized artifacts? e.g., for audit / reproducibility?
[09:04] Ellen: we record quant profile metadata, random seeds, and runtime versions in audit logs. in Private mode those logs live in your account. for high-reg compliance we recommend Private deployment.
[09:17] Sara: quick interjection — one common pattern is to keep a small dedicated pool (dedicated capacity) for sensitive routes, while letting the rest of traffic use hosted with quant. gives predictable capacity for fallbacks.
[09:30] Tom: ok can you repeat the P95 numbers for our target infra? our current P95 is 420ms on L2-13b.
[09:36] Miguel: based on your seq hist and assuming similar batcher, estimate FP32 baseline ~420ms P95, FP8 ~340ms, INT8 ~250-280ms. again these are estimates; we'd run a short prod-like bench to validate.
[09:53] Priya: let's talk about metrics for acceptance — what thresholds do you recommend?
[09:57] Miguel: typical acceptance: no more than 1.5% absolute drop in critical metric (e.g., extraction F1) across sample set, and P95 improvement target met. you can set per-route strictness.
[10:10] Ben: where can we see raw outputs to audit?
[10:13] Miguel: Optimize exports sample diffs side-by-side and you can pull raw LM outputs for human review.
[10:19] Aisha: for the pilot, can we run in our VPC and have the profiling job run there?
[10:24] Ellen: yes — Private profiling or the on-prem agent will run inside your network. we'll need a brief infra checklist — I'll send that after.
[10:33] Priya: any examples of quantization causing critical regression in production?
[10:37] Miguel: rare but yes — usually either numeric-sensitive workloads or when prompts are out-of-distribution vs the eval set. that's why per-prompt buckets and conservative rollout are important.
[10:48] Tom: what about fallback cost spikes? you mentioned simulation — will Optimize give worst-case cost if 100% of sensitive prompts fallback?
[10:54] Miguel: yes, you can simulate worst-case and expected-case. it will highlight the incremental cost of fallback and help size Dedicated capacity if needed.
[11:06] Priya: ok, security docs please.
[11:09] Sara: we'll drop the SOC2/ISO/KMS doc links in the chat and include them with the spreadsheet.
[11:15] Miguel: last demo note: we support automatic hybrid quant profiles — a profile that keeps attention weights at fp16 while compressing MLP to INT8 for a good balance. these often give 70-80% of INT8 perf with much lower quality delta.
[11:33] Ben: that hybrid approach sounds good. how much dev effort to integrate?
[11:37] Miguel: if you use our API it's mostly config changes and you can keep your routing logic. for Private, there's an agent and a small runtime integration (~1-2 engineer-weeks) depending on your infra.
[11:52] Priya: cost of Dedicated?
[11:54] Sara: i'll include Dedicated pricing tiers in the follow-up — depends on committed capacity. for pilots we can do a short-term pilot pricing.
[12:03] Tom: ok last thing, can we get a sample config for the router rules?
[12:07] Miguel: yes, i'll attach examples: JSON/YAML for per-route policies with percent rollout, fallback_model, and alert thresholds.
[12:15] Priya: sounds good. we're aligned to run a pilot. can you recap three immediate deliverables?
[12:20] Sara: sure: 1) benchmark spreadsheet and sample prompts 2) suggested quant profiles + runtime config examples 3) security/compliance docs and Dedicated pricing. we'll also schedule a pilot kickoff after you approve the eval set.
[12:35] Tom: thanks everyone, appreciate the demo.
[12:38] Priya: thanks, that was helpful. we'll meet internally and pick prompt set.
[12:42] Sara: thanks all, we'll follow up.

(End of recording)
